page.tested_text: We ran it in a normal Claude chat for **Manchester, in the UK**, with **no real name**. It listed **10 sites**, wrote **two ready-to-send requests** (one quoting the UK's right to erasure, with the one-month deadline), built a **tracker** with the date each site has to reply by, and listed **six kinds of thing that can't be removed**. Its best tip came first: most UK people-search sites get their data from the open electoral register, and you can opt out of that for free. **Not run by us:** the search for a real person's listings. We don't put anyone's name into a search for a video.
page.tip: **The tip:** send the requests from a spare email address, not your main one, and check the sites again every three months. Listings often come back.

prompt:
Act as my privacy assistant. I want my personal details taken off the internet. This is for me only: I will only give you my own name.

My name: [your full name]
Where I live: [city and country, or US state]
Old usernames or emails I've used: [optional]

Do this in order:
1. Search the web for where my details are listed. Check three kinds of places: people-search sites, data brokers, and old accounts or profiles. Only list things you actually found, with the link. If you can't search the web, say so and go to step 2.
2. Give me the 10 biggest people-search and data broker sites for where I live, each with its official opt-out or removal page.
3. For every site in steps 1 and 2, write the removal request, ready to send. Use the privacy law for where I live if there is one (for example the right to erasure in the UK and EU, or California's privacy law), and say which law you used. If no law applies, use the site's own opt-out process.
4. Build me a tracker: site, what it shows, how to remove it, date sent, and the date they must reply by.
5. Tell me honestly what can't be removed (news stories, court records, things other people posted) and what to do instead.
Never ask for my passwords, ID numbers or bank details. Start now.

followups.label: If a site ignores you
followups.prompt: It's been more than the reply-by date and [site] hasn't answered. Write my follow-up, then tell me who to complain to where I live and write that complaint too.
followups.note: In the UK that's the Information Commissioner's Office. Claude will name the right body for your country.

followups.label: Old accounts
followups.prompt: Here are the old usernames and emails I've used: [list them]. For each service I might still have an account with, give me the account-deletion page and the steps, and write the request to send if there's no button.
followups.note: For the accounts you forgot you had.

followups.label: Check again in three months
followups.prompt: Here is my tracker from last time: [paste it]. Tell me which sites to check again today and what to do if my details are back.
followups.note: Records often reappear, so save your tracker.

checklist.title: Fill in your own name and where you live
checklist.detail: The country (or US state) matters: it decides which privacy law Claude quotes.

checklist.title: Paste it into Claude with web search on
checklist.detail: It searches, lists what it found with links, then adds the biggest sites for where you live.

checklist.title: Send the requests yourself
checklist.detail: Use each site's own opt-out form first, and paste the request into it. Claude can't send anything for you.

checklist.title: Fill in the tracker
checklist.detail: Write down the date you sent each one. If the reply-by date passes, use the follow-up prompt below.

checklist.title: Check again in three months
checklist.detail: Listings often come back. Run the prompt again and compare it with your tracker.

safety: **Your own name only.** Don't use this to look anyone else up.
**You send the requests, not Claude.** It can't delete anything itself.
**Some things can't be removed:** news stories, court records, company filings, and things other people posted. The prompt tells you what to do instead.
**Don't send ID unless a site truly needs it,** and never give passwords or bank details to anyone.
**This isn't legal advice.** Privacy law is different in every country; where there is no law, sites usually still honour their own opt-out form.
**We have not run the search step on a real name.** Everything else here is from our own run.
